Explanation: The correct answer is Option B because both Patna Bird Sanctuary and Chhari-
Dhand Wetland Conservation Reserve were recently designated as Ramsar Sites. Patna Bird
Sanctuary, located in the Etah district of Uttar Pradesh, is a small but ecologically significant
freshwater wetland that becomes especially important during the winter season. It serves as a
habitat for a large number of migratory waterbirds and fulfils the Ramsar criteria for biodiversity
conservation and the protection of bird species.
Chhari-Dhand, situated in the Kutch district of Gujarat near the Banni grasslands, is a seasonal
wetland that contains both saline and freshwater pools. It supports migratory birds and desert-
adapted wildlife, making it unique among Indian wetlands. Its ecological diversity and importance
in supporting waterbird populations led to its recognition under the Ramsar Convention, an
international treaty signed in 1971 for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
Thus, since both wetlands were newly added to India’s Ramsar list, Option B is the correct
answer.
26.	Answer: B
Explanation: Statement 1: Ramsar Sites are designated under an international treaty
signed in 1971.
Status: Correct
This statement is correct because Ramsar Sites are designated under the Ramsar Convention,
which is an international treaty adopted in 1971 in the city of Ramsar, Iran.
The objective of this convention is:
Conservation of wetlands
Promotion of their “wise use”
International cooperation for shared wetland systems
Thus, whenever a wetland is declared a Ramsar Site, it means it is recognized under this 1971
international treaty framework.
Statement 2: Only freshwater wetlands can be declared as Ramsar Sites.
Status: Incorrect
This statement is incorrect because Ramsar Sites include all types of wetlands, not only
freshwater wetlands.
Under the Ramsar definition, wetlands include:

Freshwater lakes and rivers
Marshes and swamps

Mangroves
Coral reefs

Estuaries
For example:
Chilika Lake is a brackish water lagoon.
Sundarban Wetland includes mangrove ecosystems.
Chhari-Dhand Wetland Conservation Reserve has saline characteristics.
Hence, Ramsar Sites are not limited to freshwater wetlands.
Statement 3: India is a contracting party to the Ramsar Convention.
Status: Correct
India became a contracting party to the Ramsar Convention in 1982.
Being a contracting party means:
India agrees to conserve wetlands.
India commits to the wise use of wetland resources.
India must designate suitable wetlands as Ramsar Sites.
India must report conservation measures internationally.
Currently, India has one of the highest numbers of Ramsar Sites globally.

Explanation: The Sundarban Wetland, located in West Bengal, forms part of the vast Ganga—

in India recognized under the Ramsar Convention.
This wetland is globally significant because:
It is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
It is home to the iconic Royal Bengal Tiger.
It supports rich biodiversity, including estuarine crocodiles, fishing cats, migratory birds, and
diverse marine species.
It plays a crucial role in coastal protection, acting as a natural barrier against cyclones and tidal
surges.
Because of its vast size and ecological importance, it ranks as the largest Ramsar Site in India.

This means:

Explanation: The first resolution seeking the removal of a Speaker of the Lok Sabha, often
loosely referred to as a “no-confidence motion” against the Speaker, was moved in 1954. It was
directed against Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar, who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha after
the Constitution came into force. The motion was moved on 18 December 1954 by members of the
Opposition, and it was led by J. B. Kripalani. The allegation was that the Speaker was acting in a
partisan manner and not maintaining complete neutrality in the functioning of the House.
However, the motion did not succeed. It was defeated in the Lok Sabha, and G.V. Mavalankar
continued in office. Importantly, no removal motion against any Lok Sabha Speaker in Indian
parliamentary history has ever been successful. This event is significant because it demonstrated
that, although the Speaker is expected to function impartially, the office remains accountable to
the House and can be challenged through a constitutional process.
It is also important to note that the Constitution does not use the term “no-confidence motion” for
the Speaker. The correct constitutional mechanism is a resolution for removal under Article 94(c),
which requires a 14-day notice and must be passed by a majority of all the then members of the
House (effective majority). Later, similar motions were moved against Hukam Singh in 1966 and
Balram Jakhar in 1987, but none were passed. The 1954 motion therefore, holds historical
importance as the first instance of such parliamentary action against a Lok Sabha Speaker.

Explanation: The Parliament of India generally meets in three regular sessions in a year: the
Budget Session, the Monsoon Session, and the Winter Session. Although the Constitution (Article
85) does not specifically name these sessions, it mandates that there must not be a gap of more
than six months between two sittings of Parliament. Over time, by convention and practice, these
three sessions have become established as the regular working structure of Parliament. The
Budget Session is usually held from January or February to April or May and is the longest
session. It begins with the President’s Address and includes the presentation and passage of the
Union Budget. The Monsoon Session generally takes place between July and August or September
and focuses on legislative business and discussion of important national issues. The Winter
Session is typically held from November to December and deals with pending legislative matters
and urgent discussions before the year ends.
Apart from these regular sessions, Parliament can also be summoned for a Special Session, but
this is not a fixed or regular session and is called when necessary. Therefore, the three regular
sessions are Budget, Monsoon, and Winter.

Explanation: Statement 1: Retail inflation remained within the RBI’s tolerance band.
Status: Correct
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) follows a flexible inflation targeting framework with a target of
4% + 2%, meaning inflation should remain within the 2%-6% range. The Economic Survey 2025—
26 observed that headline retail inflation (CPI-based) largely stayed within this band, indicating
effective monetary policy management and supply-side measures by the government. This reflects
macroeconomic stability and controlled price pressures.
Statement 2: Food inflation was a major contributor to price volatility
Status: Correct
Food inflation was a major reason for temporary spikes in inflation. Food items such as vegetables,
cereals, and pulses are highly sensitive to:
Monsoon variations
Seasonal supply shortages
Transportation and storage disruptions
Since food has a large weight in the CPI basket (around 45%), even small price changes
significantly impact overall inflation. Hence, food inflation contributed to price volatility.
Statement 3: Core inflation increased sharply due to rising crude oil prices.
Status: Incorrect
Core inflation excludes food and fuel because they are volatile components. The Survey noted that
core inflation actually moderated, meaning underlying demand pressures in the economy were
stable. Even if crude oil prices fluctuate, fuel is excluded from core inflation calculations.
Therefore, it did not increase sharply due to crude oil prices.
43.	Answer: B
Explanation: What is Core Inflation?
Core inflation refers to the change in prices of goods and services excluding food and fuel. These
two components are removed because:
They are highly volatile.
Their prices fluctuate due to seasonal, geopolitical, or supply-side factors.
They do not always reflect underlying demand conditions in the economy.
Therefore, core inflation gives a clearer picture of structural or demand-driven inflation.
Why Exclude Food and Fuel?
1. Food prices depend on:
Monsoon performance
Crop output
Supply chain disruptions
Seasonal variations
2. Fuel prices depend on:
Global crude oil prices
Geopolitical tensions
Exchange rate fluctuations
Since these factors are often temporary or external, economists exclude them to understand the
true demand pressure in the economy.

Understanding long-term inflation trend
Identifying demand-pull inflation

Explanation: The UN High Seas Treaty is officially known as the Biodiversity Beyond National
Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. It was adopted under the framework of the United Nations and
functions as an implementing agreement to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
(UNCLOS). While UNCLOS already regulates maritime zones such as the Territorial Sea and
Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), it did not provide detailed rules for protecting biodiversity in
areas beyond national jurisdiction (the High Seas). The BBNJ Agreement fills this gap by creating
a legal mechanism for conservation, sustainable use of marine resources, environmental impact
assessments, and fair sharing of benefits from marine genetic resources.

into force on January 17, 2026, India is currently working on domestic legislation through a
specialized committee to align its national laws with the treaty’s provisions. This process of legal
adjustment is likely to delay India’s formal ratification until the necessary legislative framework
is finalized.

47.	Answer: A
Explanation: Statement 1: It is an implementing agreement under UNCLOS.
Status - Correct
The BBNJ Agreement is legally adopted under the framework of the United Nations Convention
on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). It is considered the third implementing agreement under
UNCLOS, focusing specifically on biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. Hence, this
statement is correct.
Statement 2: It provides for Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs).
Status - Correct
One of the key pillars of the treaty is making Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs)
mandatory for activities that may significantly harm marine biodiversity in the High Seas.
Therefore, this statement is also correct.
Statement 3: It gives the UN direct control over national EEZs.
Status - Incorrect
The treaty applies only to areas beyond national jurisdiction (i.e., High Seas). It does not interfere
with the sovereign rights of coastal states over their Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs). The United
Nations does not gain control over national maritime zones. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
